summary: The paper benchmarks cross-architecture representation transfer by patching translated latent operand representations from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B into Qwen2.5-14B on Python arithmetic programs. The intervention successfully drives exact numeric carry transitions across decimal boundaries across 512 evaluation groups with 100% accuracy while equal-norm random baselines fail completely. The experimental design is rigorous and highly reproducible with exact snapshot hashes and verification scripts, though the scope is tightly focused on short synthetic arithmetic additions.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including both full host-state ceiling baselines and norm-matched orthogonal random perturbation floors.
Exemplary reproducibility details provided in the text, specifying exact Hugging Face commit hashes, layer intervention positions (block 6 to block 10), and execution environment versions.
Careful parallel evaluation protocol checking greedy logit margins and valid delimiter terminations across decimal length-changing boundaries without teacher-forcing artifacts.
Strong isolation of variables by varying identifier stems and surrounding syntax between donor and host prompts.
weaknesses: Scope is limited to single-digit Python arithmetic addition programs; generality to multi-step arithmetic, other operations, or natural language reasoning remains untested.
Lacks detailed architectural discussion or mathematical description of the 7x7 linear map used to bridge the donor and host hidden representations within the text itself.
No exploration of failure boundaries, layer sensitivity sweeps, or scaling behavior across other intermediate layer pairs.
suggestions: Include a mathematical description or summary of how the 7x7 transfer map was estimated and calibrated in the text body.
Ablate the intervention across multiple donor/host layer combinations to map the representation compatibility zone beyond blocks 6 and 10.
Evaluate whether this cross-model representation surgery extends to subtraction, multiplication, or multi-digit chained additions.
